record: W05-03 P-R3-2 correction: the delivered comments described the writer epoch as observed; it is caller-supplied
reviewer_finding: P-R3-2 (reservation, accepted-with-limitations round 3): apps/cli/cli_v2.go:171-174 and apps/cli/cli_contract.go:469-475 said the epoch is 'the epoch the caller observed' and that an epoch not belonging to the current writer is refused by the core. Measured: --writer-epoch 9999 passes DecodeEnvelope and reaches the write dispatcher; client_protocol.go:152 tests presence only, and the current-writer comparison at :800-808 is on the session-attach path, which host.configure never enters. Nothing in apps/cli ever records cfg.WriterEpoch from a reply.
action: both comments rewritten to state only what is measured: absence is refused locally, presence is required by the core, the value is the caller's claim, and the 'never silent' property therefore covers omission and not invention. The obligation to anchor a model switch to an observed lease is carried forward as its own item.
why_source_and_not_the_row: cli_v2.go and cli_contract.go are product source, not registered evidence, so they can be corrected after acceptance; the accepted row's 53 evidence digests are untouched and were re-verified (task_packet next rc 0). The assertion id W0503-MODEL-CHANGE-CARRIES-THE-OBSERVED-EPOCH keeps its name even though 'observed' overstates it, because three reviewer artefacts cite that id and renaming would break their reproduction; the misnomer is disclosed here instead.
carry_forward: W05-03-epoch-is-caller-supplied: read session.get (or the attach reply) and adopt the current writer epoch before a model switch, refuse when there is no writer, and pin it with a wire-level row plus a real-core control
